#The WebAssembly JavaScript API

On this page

  • The design
  • The old form of exceptions
  • Limits

A page's own WebAssembly modules (Blazor WebAssembly, Emscripten, wasm-bindgen) run beside the engine's, on the same Wasmtime. On by default (javascript.webassembly.enabled). WebAssembly exists in windows and workers; it costs nothing until a script reads it (an auto-init property: native/js/odin/web_wasm.js is evaluated then).

Checked: a .NET 10 Blazor Web App (https://jeremyetu.azurewebsites.net/: its server circuit on the first visit, then .NET in WebAssembly with a 48 MB heap and client-side navigation), a Yew (wasm-bindgen) application, SQLite Fiddle (Emscripten in a worker), DuckDB's shell (it starts; no query was run), Pyodide (Python answers runPython), and web-platform-tests wasm/jsapi (wpt/expectations).

LayerFile
the descriptionapi/webassembly.widl (generates wj.wr_WebAssembly_* and the host table)
the browser sidesrc/page/webassembly.odin (calls) over src/wasm/user_module.odin and user_store.odin (Wasmtime)
the realm sidenative/js/odin/web_wasm.odin (the natives, the conversions of values) and web_wasm.js (the objects)
the bytes of a memoryBuffer_Host in src/engine/jsrt (b_typed.odin, object.odin), JS_NewArrayBufferHost in jscapi
the testsexamples/jsweb/webassembly.js (jsweb_webassembly), src/wasm/wasm_test.odin, src/csp/csp_test.odin, src/tools/e2e/web_jsload.odin (the policy)

web_wasm.js is the one exception to the rule of native/js/odin/prelude.odin (no JavaScript in the realm): it is not in the image, and its functions read as native ones.

#The design

  1. One store per realm. What a module imports (a memory, a table, a function of another instance) must be in its store, so everything a page makes is in one (User_Store), known to the script by numbers the host checks. It lives until the page closes, whatever the collector finds: a page that makes instances without end grows.
  2. Inside the realm's call. The store's data is the realm's instance: a module's code runs under the deadline and stop flag of the JavaScript call that entered it (wt_on_epoch). A call checks the thread's stack first (RangeError).
  3. compile off the page's thread. WebAssembly.compile, instantiate and the streaming forms compile on a thread of the blocking pool (a worker compiles on its own thread): for a 34 MB module measured, the page's timers kept running (worst gap 25 ms) where new WebAssembly.Module, synchronous as specified, blocks for the 440 ms it takes. What was compiled is kept in the profile's disk cache (wasm.cache.disk), by top-level site: what one site compiled says nothing to another.
  4. memory.buffer: an ArrayBuffer without bytes. The engine's ArrayBuffers live in its linear memory, which a page's instance cannot share, so a memory's buffer has data == nil and a Buffer_Host through which one element is one host call. The JIT and the interpreter's fast paths leave on data == nil. A builtin working on a range pins it (host_pin: a copy data points at, written back at the end, with no JavaScript running in between); set between it and the engine's memory is one call. An API of the browser gets a copy of the range of its view (JS_GetArrayBufferRange) and commits what it wrote (JS_ArrayBufferCommit: getRandomValues, encodeInto, copyTo, read). One element reads and writes a page of 4 KiB kept in the engine's memory (host_line, 16 of them): writes go back, and all is read again, when a module is entered or left and before anything else touches the bytes (host_cache_sync). Measured in a loop over 1 MiB: a read about 200 ns, a write about 330 ns (4 ns in an ordinary array, which the JIT compiles: not this path), set 0.2 ms for all of it; a call of an export 508 ns. Growing detaches the buffer, also when the module grew it (seen at the next memory.buffer).
  5. Values cross as cells (user_store.odin), converted in web_wasm.odin, so a call costs no JavaScript beyond the function called. An externref is a number in a table of web_wasm.js: the value goes when the store's collector has dropped the last reference to it (extern_released).
  6. Exceptions. One the module does not catch becomes a WebAssembly.Exception; one an import throws is thrown in the module, so it can catch it. Anything else JavaScript throws crosses under WebAssembly.JSTag: catch_all catches it, and it comes out as itself. Only the error that stops a script past its time goes through as a trap.
  7. The Content Security Policy: 'wasm-unsafe-eval' or 'unsafe-eval' where a policy has a script-src or default-src, otherwise a CompileError and a violation report. validate is not subject to it.

#The old form of exceptions

Wasmtime has exceptions as try_table; it refuses the old form (try, catch, rethrow, delegate), which browsers still take and many modules are built with. A module Wasmtime refuses goes through src/wasm/legacy_eh.odin, which rewrites it to the new form (its comment says how), and is compiled again; validate does the same. What comes out goes through Wasmtime's validation like any module, so a mistake there is a CompileError, never a wrong program, and the first error stands when the translation does not make the module valid. Checked on DuckDB's module (3.8 MB of C++), on .NET's runtime through its JIT, and by hand-written modules in the tests.

#Limits

  • Threads are in docs/shared-memory.md, with their limits. Without cross-origin isolation a page has no global SharedArrayBuffer, as in other browsers (SQLite Fiddle then says OPFS is unavailable instead of waiting on a copy).
  • GC, typed function references and memory64 follow wasm.features.* (off by default): such modules get a CompileError.
  • An exception carries at most 32 values (MAX_TAG_VALUES, web_wasm.odin).
  • Recursion through a module is bounded by the engine's stack: at the depth of recursion through a native function, far below other browsers.
  • Not there: type reflection (.type(), WebAssembly.Function), toResizableBuffer, JSPI, string builtins, source phase imports; other realms' prototypes for new.target from another realm.
